profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, traded under the ticker NVDA. Its site presents the NVIDIA Nemotron family of multimodal models as built for agentic reasoning in graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding. The company describes Nemotron as a family of efficient, multimodal, open AI models intended for long-running, self-evolving agents, with transparent training data and support across platforms including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the vision behind Nemotron and on open technologies for enterprise AI.

Nemotron models are offered as NVIDIA NIM microservices for inference and deployment, which the company says requires an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, and models and microservices can be tried and downloaded from build.nvidia.com. The company says it publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, described as a permissive license allowing use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. Other tools named on the site include NVIDIA NeMo for custom agentic AI, NVIDIA Blueprints for reference workflows, NVIDIA Dynamo, and TensorRT-LLM, along with the open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard are described as helping agents complete specialized tasks faster and routing each step to the right model. The site also lists Nemotron Speech models for automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding, embeddings, and ranking. ServiceNow appears among the partners named.

NVIDIA's most recent annual report on Form 10-K covers a period ending January 25, 2026, and reports revenue of $215,938,000,000. Its CIK is 0001045810. Litigation tracked for the company totals 270 cases in California.
